learn.hook: At the top of Mount Everest, the air has only about one-third as much oxygen as at sea level!
points: 'Conquering the Summit' is about mountaineering and the grit it takes to reach the top.
Mount Everest (8,849 m) is the highest mountain in the world. It lies on the border of Nepal and China (Tibet).
Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary were the first to reach its summit, on 29 May 1953.
Bachendri Pal became the first Indian woman to climb Everest, in 1984.
Mountaineering words: summit, base camp, expedition, altitude, ice axe, crampons, oxygen cylinder.

example.q: Why do climbers on very high mountains carry oxygen cylinders?
steps: Altitude means height above sea level.
The higher you go, the thinner the air, so there is less oxygen in each breath.
Extra oxygen helps climbers breathe and stay safe.
example.answer: Because the air at great heights has much less oxygen, so they carry extra oxygen to breathe safely.

learn.reallife: Mountaineering institutes in Darjeeling, Uttarkashi and Manali train young climbers in safety and teamwork.

games.title: Mountain words
pairs: the highest point of a mountain
the main camp at the foot of a mountain
a journey made for a special purpose
metal spikes fixed to boots for walking on ice

games.title: A climbing expedition
items: Train for months to get fit.
Get used to the thin air at higher camps.

quiz.q: What does 'summit' mean?
options: the highest point of a mountain
quiz.explain: The summit is the very top of a mountain.
quiz.mistake: Confuses summit with other mountain words

quiz.q: What is the height of Mount Everest?
quiz.explain: Everest's height was measured as 8,849 metres in 2020.
quiz.mistake: Remembers the digits but not the thousands

quiz.q: Who were the first to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953?
quiz.explain: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reached the top on 29 May 1953.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up famous explorers

quiz.q: Who was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest?
quiz.explain: Bachendri Pal reached the summit in 1984.
quiz.mistake: Picks another famous Indian woman from a different field

quiz.q: What is a 'base camp'?
options: the main camp at the foot of a mountain where climbers start and rest
a school for mountaineers in a city
quiz.explain: Climbers gather supplies and rest at base camp before climbing.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the base with the top

quiz.q: Why do climbers on Everest carry oxygen?
options: The air at great heights has less oxygen
quiz.explain: Higher up, the air is thinner, so each breath has less oxygen.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how altitude affects air

quiz.q: What does 'expedition' mean?
options: a journey made for a special purpose
quiz.explain: Mountain climbs and explorations are called expeditions.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word

quiz.q: Mount Everest lies on the border of:
quiz.explain: Everest is on the Nepal–China (Tibet) border.
quiz.mistake: Assumes Everest is in India

teach.ask: Gappu wants to fly over Mount Everest. Tell him about climbing it.
teach.praise: Wow! 8,849 metres! I'll wave at the climbers when I fly past!
teach.nudge: Who climbed Everest first, and what is its top called?

learn.hook: Add '-ation' to 'determine' and you get the one word every mountaineer needs: determination!
points: Determination is a strong will to reach your goal, even when it is hard.
Suffixes are added at the end of a word and can change its class: determine → determination, achieve → achievement.
-ous, -ful and -less make adjectives: courage → courageous, hope → hopeful, fear → fearless. (-ful = full of; -less = without)
-ly makes many adverbs: brave → bravely, tireless → tirelessly.
A character's actions show their qualities: trying again every day shows determination.

example.q: Read: When Pema first tried to climb the hill behind her school in Sikkim, she stopped halfway, out of breath. The next morning, she tried again. Every day she climbed a little higher, carrying her water bottle and a smile. By winter, she reached the top without stopping and saw the snowy peaks glowing in the sun. Which quality does Pema show, and which words prove it?
steps: 'The next morning, she tried again.' and 'Every day she climbed a little higher.'
She did not give up until she reached the top.
example.answer: Determination — she tried again every day until she reached the top.

learn.reallife: Athletes, students preparing for exams and farmers waiting for the monsoon all need determination.

quiz.q: What is the noun form of 'determine'?
quiz.explain: The suffix -ation turns the verb 'determine' into the noun 'determination'.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the noun with other forms

quiz.q: What is the adjective formed from 'courage'?
quiz.explain: Courage + -ous = courageous (full of courage).
quiz.mistake: Adds the wrong suffix

quiz.q: What does 'hopeless' mean?
quiz.explain: The suffix -less means 'without'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up -less and -ful

quiz.q: What is the noun formed from 'achieve'?
quiz.explain: Achieve + -ment = achievement.
quiz.mistake: Uses a suffix that does not form a noun from this verb

quiz.q: 'When Pema first tried to climb the hill, she stopped halfway. The next morning, she tried again.' Pema is:
quiz.explain: She keeps trying after failing — she is determined.
quiz.mistake: Focuses only on her first failure

quiz.q: What does 'fearless' mean?
quiz.explain: -less means without, so fearless means having no fear.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the meaning of the suffix

quiz.q: 'The climbers worked ___ to reach the top.'
quiz.explain: We need an adverb to describe how they worked: tirelessly.
quiz.mistake: Uses an adjective where an adverb is needed

quiz.q: 'Every day Pema climbed a little higher. By winter, she reached the top without stopping.' What helped Pema succeed?
quiz.explain: She climbed a little higher every day — regular practice.
quiz.mistake: Picks a reason not given in the text

teach.ask: Gappu keeps quitting his flying lessons. What does determination mean, and which suffix turns 'determine' into a noun?
teach.praise: With determination, I'll reach the highest branch! And -ation makes it a noun!
teach.nudge: What does a determined person do, and which ending do we add?

learn.hook: 'She has climbed Everest!' — the present perfect connects a past action to right now.
points: Present perfect = has/have + past participle: She has climbed. They have reached.
Use 'has' with he, she, it and singular nouns; 'have' with I, you, we, they and plural nouns.
It is used for actions finished at an unstated time or with a result now; words like just, already, yet, ever, never go with it.
Do not use it with a definite past time (yesterday, in 1953) — use simple past: 'Tenzing and Hillary reached the summit in 1953.'
'Since' + a point of time (since 2019); 'for' + a length of time (for six months).

example.q: Choose correctly: 'Riya (has reached / reached) base camp yesterday.'
steps: The present perfect is not used with a definite past time.

learn.reallife: News headlines often use the present perfect: 'Indian team has won the gold!'

games.title: Since or for? Has or have?
Present perfect rules
items: 'Has' is used with he, she and it.
He has climbed; she has climbed.
The present perfect uses has/have + past participle.
For example: have seen, has gone.
'I have climbed the hill yesterday' is correct.
With 'yesterday' we use simple past: 'I climbed the hill yesterday.'
'Since' is used with a point of time, like 'since Monday'.
'For' is used with a length of time.
'Went' is the simple past; the past participle is 'gone'.

quiz.q: 'Riya ___ just reached base camp.'
quiz.explain: Riya is singular, so we use 'has' + reached.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'have' with a singular subject

quiz.q: 'We ___ climbed this hill many times.'
quiz.explain: 'We' takes 'have' in the present perfect.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'has' with a plural subject

quiz.q: Which sentence about the 1953 climb is correct?
options: Tenzing and Hillary has reached the summit in 1953.
Tenzing and Hillary have reached the summit in 1953.
Tenzing and Hillary reaching the summit in 1953.
Tenzing and Hillary reached the summit in 1953.
quiz.explain: 'In 1953' is a definite past time, so simple past is used.
quiz.mistake: Uses present perfect with a definite past time

quiz.q: 'I have lived in Shimla ___ 2020.'
quiz.explain: 2020 is a point of time, so we use 'since'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up since and for

quiz.q: 'The team has trained ___ three months.'
quiz.explain: Three months is a length of time, so we use 'for'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'since' with a length of time

quiz.q: What is the past participle of 'go'?
quiz.explain: go – went – gone. 'Gone' goes with has/have.
quiz.mistake: Uses the simple past form instead of the past participle

quiz.q: Which sentence is in the present perfect tense?
quiz.explain: Has + finished (past participle) is present perfect.
quiz.mistake: Confuses present perfect with simple past

quiz.q: 'Have you ever ___ snow?'
quiz.explain: After 'have', we need the past participle: see – saw – seen.
quiz.mistake: Uses the simple past after 'have'

teach.ask: Gappu says, 'I have flew to the hill yesterday.' Fix it and explain the present perfect.
teach.praise: 'I flew to the hill yesterday' — and 'I have flown to many hills!' Got it!
teach.nudge: What form of the verb comes after 'have', and what tense goes with 'yesterday'?
